title: We’re all Eurorealists now
gist: Ten years after Brexit, De Vries and Kentikelenis argue the EU's slow, veto-laden model delivers 'effective sovereignty', Eurosceptics have retreated from exit, and Britain's formal autonomy has cost it practical control, shifting UK debate toward the single market.

insights.claim: None of the feared Brexit contagion (Frexit, Nexit, Italexit) has materialised, and nearly three quarters of Europeans say their country has benefitted from EU membership according to Eurobarometer.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: EU breakup tail risk has proved overstated.
insights.locator: A decade later, not one of these fears

insights.claim: Europe's radical right has moved from hard Euroscepticism to changing the EU from within: Le Pen dropped her referendum pledge, Wilders shifted away from Dutch exit, and Meloni presents Italian and European interests as intertwined.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Populist electoral wins imply EU reform pressure, not exit.

insights.claim: Brexit helped discredit exit just as continental Eurosceptics turned to changing the EU from within, and arrived just before geopolitical change made European cooperation more consequential.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Structural drift in Europe favours cooperation over exit.
insights.locator: Brexit thus leaves us with two ironies

insights.claim: The EU does not move one-way toward a superstate; it stalls, backtracks and allows opt-outs, and Britain with its rebate and opt-outs was the chief beneficiary of that flexibility.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Challenges the framing underlying Leave arguments.
insights.locator: The truth is that the EU has never moved in one direction

insights.claim: The EU's slowness and multiple veto points make it hard to capture, in contrast to the US where a narrow majority in a handful of states can hand one person power to rewrite foreign policy within weeks.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Institutional friction makes EU policy more durable and predictable than US policy.

insights.claim: Effective sovereignty means the collective ability of Europeans acting through common institutions to shape outcomes states cannot control alone, such as terms of trade with Washington or Beijing and AI standards.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Pooled bargaining weight is the EU's economic value proposition amid US-China rivalry.
insights.quote: sovereignty is more about the ability to shape events than the imaginary freedom to decide alone
insights.locator: The deeper misunderstanding of the EU

insights.claim: Post-Brexit Britain regained formal autonomy but not practical control: exporters follow European standards they no longer help set, and issues like food standards, educational exchange and defence access are now negotiated slowly and expensively with Brussels.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: UK-EU reset negotiations are a continuing driver of UK trade and regulatory outcomes.
insights.quote: Taking back control often meant less effective sovereignty.
insights.locator: After Brexit, formal autonomy was recovered in full

insights.claim: UK opinion has shifted: per YouGov half of Britons support rejoining the single market and customs union and 59 per cent favour a closer EU relationship, including 54 per cent of Leave voters; Major and Osborne now back rejoining the single market or customs union.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Rising odds of closer UK-EU economic alignment; Burnham has floated going 'all the way'.
insights.locator: The change in Britain’s political debate is telling

insights.claim: Trump's return and Russia's war on Ukraine have undermined the assumption that the US will indefinitely underwrite European security, raising the stakes of European cooperation for Britain.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Supports European defence integration and spending themes.
insights.locator: The world around Britain has changed too

insights.claim: US-China strategic competition treats trade, technology and finance as statecraft instruments, and states acting alone risk becoming 'vassal states' that inherit decisions made elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
insights.so_what: Smaller powers face pressure to pick sides; blocs gain value.

source_meta.author: Catherine E De Vries and Alexandros Kentikelenis
